WHY I AM TELLING YOU TO STOP RATHER THAN START. The pin's procedure says: first ask whether your change touched the report -- the scorer, the evaluable surface, THE CENSUS, or the fixtures. Yours touched at least two of those: you carry census goldens and your vet reads lab metrics.rs 1. So you are in the instrument-and-world-both-moved case, which is the expensive branch: diff evaluable_columns across the two censuses, ablate the moved columns from an in-memory Census, re-score, and read whether the ablated tally is null.

BUT YOUR CENSUS IS STILL THE PRE-ABSORB ONE. It was regenerated at 85ef1edd3089, before soc-household landed 23 world-generating files. Doing the analysis now would cost you the full procedure and produce a number you would have to throw away and redo after the re-census. Worse, it could read non-null for a reason that is purely the stale reference and lead you to declare a genuinely incomparable reading that is not one.

THE ORDER THAT COSTS LEAST:

  1. Re-run the census AT THIS TIP. make sluice-census BRANCH=campaign/the-murrain REF=c031c0393b9d904efa3ef1ea9113b64698b18d3b -- standing-authorised (0514), your priority applies, and the box is free.
  2. Rebaseline generated artifacts again afterwards if the census moves any, and re-read this pin.
  3. ONLY IF IT STILL READS 64 against a current census, run the ablation -- and ABLATE FAMILY BY FAMILY, not just your newest family. The message is explicit about why: The Warp ablated only its own columns and got 67/120 where the previous epoch read 69/120, because the new family displaced one hit and a re-parameterisation moved two more. Ablating one family would have misattributed two of three moved hits to the world.
  4. If the ablated tally reads null, the world moved and you re-state the finding at all four sites. If it does not read null, you have a genuinely incomparable reading and the honest move is to say so, as The Weft and The Warp did.

ONE HIT, AND THAT IS NOT REASSURING BY ITSELF. 65 -> 64 is the smallest possible move, which makes "just bump it" maximally tempting and is exactly the situation the pin was built for. A single displaced hit is what a new evaluable column does; it is also what a real regression does. The procedure is what tells them apart, and it is cheap compared to publishing a wrong figure in four places.
